paper_title: Spectral Editing of Activations for Large Language Model Alignment
caption: : Left: Accuracy of all methods on each group of bias type in BBQ. Right: results on BBQ's testing set. All methods are applied on LLaMA-2-Chat-7B. For accuracy (A%_{}), higher values are better; for unknown-answer response rate (U%_{}), bias score (BS%_{}) and stereotypical response rate (SR%_{}), lower is better. We use bold font for the best result in each column, and mark the methods that improve ICL. : significant improvements on ICL in A% by pair-wise t-test with p < 0.05.
model_annotation: The line plot, titled “TruthfulQA,” illustrates the performance of three methods—Linear SAE, LLaMA-2-chat-7B, and ICD—on the TruthfulQA benchmark as a function of the number of demonstrations, ranging from 0 to 2000. The x-axis, labeled “#Demonstrations,” is linearly scaled with tick marks at 0, 500, 1000, 1500, and 2000. The y-axis, labeled “MCI” (likely Meaningful Correctness Index or a similar metric), spans from 37 to 39.5, with major gridlines at 37, 38, and 39. The “Linear SAE” method is represented by a solid dark blue line with circular markers; it begins at approximately MCI = 37.1 at 0 demonstrations, rises to ~38.0 by 500, fluctuates slightly around 38.1–38.2 up to 1500, then sharply increases to ~39.3 at 2000 demonstrations. The “LLaMA-2-chat-7B” baseline is shown as a dashed magenta line with no markers, remaining nearly flat at MCI ≈ 37.0 across all demonstration counts. The “ICD” method is depicted as a dotted cyan line with no markers, staying constant at MCI ≈ 37.8 across the entire range. A horizontal cyan dashed line labeled “ICD (Prompt version)” is drawn at MCI ≈ 37.8, indicating a baseline performance level for that variant. The plot visually emphasizes the strong upward trend of Linear SAE with increasing demonstrations, while the other two methods show no improvement.
